caption:
Anthropic launched Claude Ship, a set of AI agents that review, fix and approve routine code changes on GitHub.
One agent, Claude Approvals, can approve pull requests on its own when they meet rules a team writes in plain language.
It is in beta for Claude Team and Enterprise plans.

paragraphs.text: Anthropic launched Claude Ship on November 23, 2026, a suite of AI agents that automates code reviews, fixes and approvals for routine code changes. The product is in beta and is available for repositories on GitHub to customers on Claude Team and Enterprise plans, according to TechCrunch and Digital Trends.

Claude Ship has three parts. Code Review, which checks pull requests, was already generally available. The two new pieces, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, are in beta. Anthropic positions the bundle as a way for early adopters to review pull requests and decide which ones are ready to merge.
What the two new agents do

PR Steward works on problems in a pull request after it is opened. It handles failing continuous integration checks, merge conflicts and feedback from Code Review. After each push, it leaves a comment explaining what it changed and how to roll the change back. Developers can give it more instructions by mentioning @claude or stop it with "@claude stop". PR Steward cannot approve or merge pull requests, Digital Trends reported.

Claude Approvals is the part that can approve code automatically. It applies an approval policy that a team writes in natural language and stores as a file in the repository. The policy can draw on signals such as Code Review findings or a company's own classifiers. Digital Trends gave the example of a policy that approves documentation changes while still requiring a human to approve sensitive code.

In its blog post, Anthropic said most teams want a person to approve every change and noted that Claude now writes most of the code on its own Claude Code team, TechCrunch reported. The company framed automated approval as a response to that shift.
How teams start and what it costs

Developers can begin by updating Claude Code and running a new /ship command when their code is ready. Claude then pushes the changes, opens a pull request, reviews the code and works on the issues it finds. Teams can also enable the process for a whole repository so it starts automatically.

Because the agents are in beta, Anthropic suggests running them in an observe-only mode first, starting with a single repository and setting monthly spending limits. Teams choose where Claude Ship runs, which review depth to use among Quick, Standard and Deep, and which changes are escalated to a human. Usage is billed by tokens, so costs grow with the amount of work Claude does.

Some organizations cannot use the product yet. According to Digital Trends, customers using Zero Data Retention are excluded, as are organizations with HIPAA configurations or customer-managed encryption keys.

Claude Ship moves AI coding tools from writing code toward deciding what ships. As agents produce more code than people can comfortably review, the bottleneck shifts to approval, and Anthropic is betting that teams will hand routine sign-offs to a model under written rules. The observe-only default and spending caps suggest the company expects cautious adoption at first.

The key thing to watch is whether engineering teams actually let Claude Approvals merge changes without a human, and whether Anthropic extends Claude Ship beyond GitHub and its Team and Enterprise plans.
